title: Standardize embedding scoring primitives and client migration shim
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Several downstream consumers (internal and external) rely on embedding similarity scores but observe inconsistent behavior when clients switch models or when inputs are unnormalized. We have historically supported both raw dot-product scores and cosine-normalized scores; some SDKs and legacy clients assume L2-normalized embeddings while others do not. This has caused incorrect reranking in a few customer reports and makes A/B rollouts risky. Goal: provide a clear, backward-compatible runtime primitive and an opt-in migration/shim that ensures deterministic scoring semantics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while minimizing latency impact.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a first-class scoring primitive in the runtime (score_mode) that can be one of: dot, cosine, dot_scaled (dot with explicit L2 scale metadata).
Add an opt-in request header X-Redwood-Embed-Score to allow clients to assert the desired scoring semantics for that request (values: dot | cosine | auto).
Implement a server-side compatibility shim (opt-in via account flag) that detects legacy clients and applies a transparent normalization/scaling step without changing stored embedding vectors.
All existing clients default to previous behavior (backwards compatible) unless they opt into the new header or account flag.
End-to-end latency regression <= 3% p50 and <= 6% p95 for the rerank endpoint when the shim or cosine mode is active (measured on standard 8k-op benchmark).
Add telemetry: per-request score_mode, pre/post normalization L2 norms distribution, and a compatibility-shim hit metric to the Console. Dashboards and alerts created.
Provide migration docs and SDK helpers for Python/TS to opt into 'cosine' and to verify scores against a golden set.
Run canary rollout across 3 accounts and observe no regression in relevance metrics (NDCG@10 change < 0.5% absolute) before wide release.
implementation_notes: Runtime changes: add score_mode field to internal request proto and expose a thin header mapping. Keep the default null path to preserve exact legacy behavior.

Normalization approach: use fast L2 normalization fused with KV-cache lookup on decode paths for minimal overhead. For batch rerank (N queries x M candidates), compute candidate norms once per batch and reuse.
dot_scaled semantics: preserve raw dot magnitude but attach a per-embedding scale value (L2 norm) in metadata so that consumers can compute cosine offline. This avoids rewriting stored embeddings.

Compatibility shim: when enabled for an account, server will auto-detect client SDK version via User-Agent + API key metadata; if legacy client and request has no X-Redwood-Embed-Score header, apply server-side L2-normalization before scoring.
SDK changes: add helper compute_cosine and verify_score_mode helpers. Provide a migration script to sample production queries and compare old vs new ranking outputs and norms.
Testing: unit tests for score_mode conversions, fuzz tests with random embeddings to ensure no NaNs, and integration tests in dedicated+private with quantized embeddings to ensure numeric stability.

Perf: benchmarked C++ fused kernel for normalization: median cost ~ 45ns per vector on A100; end-to-end p95 increase measured at 4.8% in worst case for 128-d embeddings under heavy batching; optimizations planned (SIMD path for CPU fallback).
rollout_plan: Step 1 (Dev): Implement score_mode proto and header, add unit tests, and land SDK helpers. (ENG owner)
Step 2 (Canary): Enable compatibility-shim for two internal accounts + one small external customer. Monitor telemetry for 72 hours (latency, NDCG, and shim_hit_rate).
Step 3 (Staged): Offer account opt-in via Console toggle; run a 2-week staged roll where 10% of new customers default to 'auto' scoring. Collect relevance and latency metrics.
Step 4 (Docs + SDK): Publish migration guide, sample scripts for verifying ranking parity, and add 'score_mode' flag to client SDKs (Python/TS/Go).

Step 5 (GA): Flip default for new API keys to expose the header but maintain legacy default behavior until 2026-09-01. Provide opt-in deprecation warnings to customers that rely on legacy implicit semantics.
metrics: Latency goals: p50 <= baseline * 1.03, p95 <= baseline * 1.06 when normalization is applied.
Quality goals: NDCG@10 regression < 0.5% absolute on held-out eval prompt sets used by Search and Rerank teams.
Telemetry events: embed.score_mode, embed.pre_norm_mean, embed.pre_norm_p95, embed.post_norm_mean, shim.hit_count
Canary dashboards: per-account NDCG, mismatch rate between client-side score and server-side score, shim latency contribution (ms).
